response.sql:
WITH rep_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    e.EmployeeId,
    e.City,
    COUNT(c.CustomerId) as customer_count
  FROM Employee e
  INNER JOIN Customer c ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.City
),
with_city_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    *,
    AVG(customer_count) OVER (PARTITION BY City) as city_avg,
    SUM(customer_count) OVER () as grand_total
  FROM rep_counts
),
above_avg AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM with_city_avg
  WHERE customer_count > city_avg
)
SELECT 
  City,
  SUM(customer_count) as total_customers_in_city,
  AVG(CAST(customer_count AS DECIMAL) - city_avg) as avg_above_city_average,
  AVG(CAST(customer_count AS DECIMAL) / grand_total) as avg_share_of_total
FROM above_avg
GROUP BY City
ORDER BY City

assumptions.assumption: "Overall customer total" is the sum of customers across all support reps in the database, not limited to only those reps who are above average in their cities
